new:
Humanoid is not inserted into `motion_model_sources` as a fake model target. A portable `HumanoidMotion` has different identity and lifetime semantics from a concrete model-specific Native output. Instead, import owns one optional canonical Humanoid variant for each logical motion and exposes it beside the concrete outputs as `a / Humanoid`.

For VMD and other motion-only sources, the importer needs one stable Humanoid-capable model provenance to convert the motion into semantic Humanoid space. The implementation therefore adds an optional persisted `motion_humanoid_source_model` provenance for motion-only import settings. When `motion_original_model_source` is present and structurally Humanoid-usable it is the natural default; otherwise an associated concrete model may be selected as the Humanoid source. The selected provenance must be a registered model source with a usable HumanoidProfile. Target-list ordering is not semantic and must never choose the Humanoid source implicitly.

Once that provenance is valid, the same import/reimport operation that emits target-specific Native clips also emits the single canonical `HumanoidMotion` for the logical motion. If no valid Humanoid source model/profile exists, import emits only the concrete Native candidates and no `a / Humanoid` row. Adding or selecting a valid Humanoid source and reimporting creates the portable candidate before any Animation Set uses it. Scene resolution and the Animation Set picker never create the HumanoidMotion as a side effect.

Changing the Humanoid source provenance is an import-content change and regenerates the portable motion and its dependent derived bakes. It does not create `a / Humanoid (x)` and `a / Humanoid (y)` rows: one logical motion owns at most one portable Humanoid candidate at a time.
